transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

First off, take a deep breath! Your fridge is almost certainly not faulty. What you are describing is completely normal operation for this specific model (and most modern refrigerators).

The Bosch KGN36VLEAG is a NoFrost fridge-freezer with advanced cooling technology. The noises your husband hears are typical acoustic signatures of its internal components working correctly. Here’s what each sound likely means:

### 1. Gurgling/Bubbling Sound (Like Water Running)
• Cause: This is the refrigerant circulating through the evaporator coils inside the fridge compartment. As the liquid refrigerant turns into gas to absorb heat, it creates this flowing/gurgling noise.
• Is it normal? Yes. It’s especially noticeable when the compressor has just switched off or during defrost cycles.

### 2. Clicking Sound (Every So Often)
• Cause: This is usually one of two things:
• Thermostat/Relay Switching: The control system clicking as it engages or disengages the compressor or fans.
• Ice Melting/Drip: During a defrost cycle, ice melts and drops onto the hot evaporator plate below, causing a small “ping” or click.
• Is it normal? Yes. This is part of the automatic NoFrost defrost process.

### 3. Crackling/Popping Noise at Night
• Cause: This is caused by thermal expansion and contraction. The interior plastic liners, shelves, and components expand when warm air enters (e.g., after you open the door) or contract as they cool down overnight. At night, when the house is quiet and the fridge is in a steady cooling phase, these tiny shifts become audible.
• Is it normal? Yes. This is very common in new fridges and often decreases slightly over time as materials settle.

---

### Why It Might Feel Louder Now
• New Installation: The fridge may have been moved or tilted during delivery, which can sometimes cause temporary changes in how sounds travel until everything settles into its final position.
• Quiet Environment: At night, background noise is lower, making normal operational sounds seem louder.
• Leveling Issues: If the fridge isn’t perfectly level, vibrations from the compressor can amplify noises. Check that all four feet are firmly on the ground and adjustable if needed.

---

### When to Actually Worry (Red Flags)
While the sounds you described are normal, contact Bosch Customer Service or your retailer if you notice:
• A loud, continuous humming or buzzing that doesn’t stop.
• Grinding, screeching, or metallic knocking noises (could indicate a fan hitting something).
• The fridge is not cooling properly (food spoiling quickly).
• Water pooling inside the fridge or leaking onto the floor (beyond normal condensation during defrost).

---

### What You Can Do Now
1. Reassure Your Husband: Explain that these sounds are signs the fridge is working correctly, not failing. Many people mistake normal operation for faults when buying a new appliance.
2. Check Leveling: Use a spirit level to ensure the fridge is perfectly upright and stable. Adjust the front feet if needed.
3. Give It Time: Sometimes, noises diminish slightly after the first few weeks as components settle.
4. Document If Needed: If the noise is truly unbearable (though it sounds normal), you can record a video of the sound at night to show Bosch support for peace of mind—but they will likely confirm it’s within acceptable limits.

Bottom Line: Your Bosch KGN36VLEAG is behaving exactly as designed. It’s not faulty! 🎉 If your husband remains concerned, you can always call Bosch Customer Care (UK: 0345 678 9012) to speak with a technician who can confirm this over the phone—they hear these questions often and will reassure him too.
